title: Microsoft Purview DLP: SLA-based alert reporting dashboard
summary: Hold: the briefing omits a documented lower-tier-plus-add-on licensing route for aggregated alerts and a restriction on selecting severity None. It also labels the unpublished SLA control tenant-wide and asserts that no budget control applies without supporting documentation. The roadmap dates and planned dashboard capabilities match the record.

claims.claim: MTTD conventionally means mean time to detect.

claims.claim: MTTR conventionally means mean time to respond or resolve.

claims.claim: Aggregated alerts based on a threshold need a higher subscription tier such as A5, E5 or G5.
claims.quote: An E1, F1, or G1 subscription or an E3 or G3 subscription that includes one of the following features:
claims.fix: Replace the aggregated-alert licensing statement in both places with: 'Aggregated alert configuration requires A5, E5 or G5, or E1, F1, G1, E3 or G3 with Office 365 Advanced Threat Protection Plan 2, Microsoft Purview Suite, or the Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.' claims.fix: Remove 'No cap or budget control applies, because no meter is documented.' The preceding absence of a published dashboard meter does not establish that budget controls cannot apply.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -ReportSeverityLevel High sets a DLP rule's incident-report severity.
claims.quote:
The ReportSeverityLevel parameter specifies the severity level of the incident report for content detections based on the rule. Valid values are:
- None: You can't select this value if the rule has no actions configured.
- Low: This value is the default.
- Medium
- High

claims.claim: The severity setting under Incident reports is labelled Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports.
claims.quote:
Under Incident reports:
1. Set Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports to Low.

claims.claim: Rule severity is an existing DLP incident-report setting, distinct from an undocumented SLA dashboard configuration.
